author: TEDx Talks
description:
Pain tolerance varies from person to person, though it’s never really been understood why. That’s what makes Kevin’s investigation into the endocannabinoid system so impactful. In this talk, he describes how his research into endocannabinoids, naturally occurring compounds  in the body structurally similar to cannabis, act like breaks that dampen pain-processing and how this can be used in the chronic pain management.  Kevin's path to pain research started in the clinic. As a physiotherapist working across Ireland over, he treated hundreds of patients and noticed something striking: people with nearly identical injuries often had completely different pain experiences.
This observation led him to a fundamental question: what makes some people more sensitive to pain than others?

Now pursuing his PhD at the University of Galway under Professor, Kevin is investigating the endocannabinoid system—a biological network that helps regulate pain, stress, mood and numerous other bodily function
title: The endocannabinoid system and your pain tolerance | Kevin Murray | TEDxGalway

In this talk, she argues that boredom is not a problem to fix but a superpower to protect, one that gives the brain the space it needs to wander, connect ideas, and create. description: Most of us spend hours connecting with friends online but struggle to find that same spark at home. In this talk, eighth grader Aria Wang makes the case that three simple word games can do what social media cannot: bring families together through laughter, surprise, and shared silliness. Word games, she argues, are not just entertainment but a language of connection hiding in plain sight. Aria is an 8th grader who loves word games and the connections they create. She enjoys bringing her family together for “game nights,” where favorites like Hangman, Mad Libs, and Telephone spark laughter, creativity, and unexpected discoveries. Through these simple games, Aria believes families can learn more about one another, strengthen their bonds, and turn ordinary moments into memorable experiences. description: In New York City, millions of pounds of food move through the world's largest wholesale produce market every day, yet 1.2 million residents still go hungry. Rishi Amin argues that hunger isn't a supply problem, it's a logistics problem rooted in where food is, when it's available, and how it gets to people. By redesigning the systems that move food, not producing more of it, we can close the gap between abundance and access. #Aging #Caregiving #FutureOfHealth #LongevityPlanning

Most people don’t fail at aging because they don’t care—they fail because no one ever taught them how to prepare. In this TEDx talk, gerontologist and former journalist Susanna Barton reframes aging not as decline, but as a design challenge we can plan for—together.

We plan carefully for careers, families, and finances—but we leave aging to chance. Drawing from lived caregiving experience and demographic data, this talk argues that earlier, intentional planning reduces chaos, cost, and emotional burden later. Aging isn’t a crisis waiting to happen—it’s a system we can design with foresight.

Why This Matters Now: People are living longer than ever. Centenarians are rapidly increasing. Older adults now outnumber children in many countries. description: This talk takes audiences from the International Space Station to the hospital bedside, revealing how the extreme environment of space is accelerating the future of medicine on Earth. Drawing on pioneering research in brain health, wearable monitoring, disease modeling, and in-space biomanufacturing, it shows how microgravity is unlocking breakthroughs in human performance, cancer research, drug discovery, and tissue engineering. From protein crystals that improve life-saving therapies to the first clinically annotated tumors grown in orbit, space is becoming a powerful new laboratory for improving human health. As the talk reveals, space isn’t just a place for a few to explore. Rather, it’s an environment where exciting discoveries can be made and brought back to Earth for the benefit of everyone.
